item.text: {"text":"Evidence supports testing the loss before adding context corruption. [gSASRec (2024)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) attributes much of the SASRec–BERT4Rec gap to overconfidence from negative-sampled BCE; its transferable idea is calibrated gBCE with more negatives, while retaining BERT4Rec. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) finds that standard sampling correction mishandles the deterministically included positive. Its revised loss uses corrected negative logits and a detached uncertainty weight. Public experiments use SASRec, so gains for masked BERT4Rec remain a hypothesis. [Improved Rank Estimation (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) provides sampling-bias corrections for WARP/LambdaRank, offering another ranking-oriented objective.\n\nFalse-negative handling addresses a separate problem from proposal-distribution correction. [UFNRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) identifies suspected false negatives and supplies teacher soft labels, but its teacher mechanism is unsuitable for this experiment’s single-model constraint. A compatible first ablation would exclude known training-history positives and target collisions from sampled negatives; treating other high-scoring items as false negatives remains uncertain. Compare the supplied loss against full-softmax CE where affordable, multi-negative sampled CE with explicit sampling probabilities, revised logQ, and calibrated gBCE. Hold leakage-free terminal prefixes, appended-mask inference, seeds and training limits fixed; report GPU time alongside macro validation HR@10. These are proposed comparisons, not demonstrated improvements on the four Amazon categories. Sampling choices deserve separate controls: a [2024 sequential-recommendation study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) found substantial dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-bias tradeoffs."}
